A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FiPS research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A.1–A.2 are readable and support reliable matching across additions, relocations, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original FiPS compression and transfer-learning results, alongside reconstruction experiments and component ablations in Sections 2, 4, and 5.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds structured-sparsity accuracy comparisons and measured GPU/CPU latency and memory results.

M1.justification: v2 extends FiPS to N:M-structured sparsification, including structured GMP and RigL variants. This changes the sparsification constraint for these variants, while the shared SVD initialization, reconstruction objective, core Algorithm 1, and original unstructured recipe remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-1k, CIFAR-100, Flowers102, Oxford Pets, and iNaturalist 2019 for the same classification and transfer tasks. The new sparsity and hardware experiments retain this vision-model coverage; they change configurations and evaluation procedures.

E2.justification: v2 adds a structured-sparsity comparison family in Table 3: STE, SR-STE, NMSRigL, and NMSGMP, evaluated alongside unstructured FiPS. The AAFM/GFM comparisons and existing dense, static-sparsity, and RigL comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols evaluate structured methods at 50% sparsity and profile end-to-end latency and VRAM across batch sizes, parameter budgets, and storage formats. GPU profiling uses 2:4 sparsity, CPU profiling uses 75% unstructured sparsity, and latency budgets are adjusted for compatible tensor dimensions. Previously reported training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 3 adds an analysis of the accuracy cost of structured sparsity and alternative sparsification algorithms. Figure 5 adds practical efficiency analyses across batch sizes, budgets, and sparse storage representations. The earlier initialization, grouping, pruning, calibration, and neuron-growth analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added experiments continue point-estimate reporting, and the existing Pearson correlation analysis is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and v1 Table 3/v2 Table 4 retain their numerical results, as do the existing plots. v2 adds latency/VRAM measurements and structured-sparsity accuracy rows. For example, at a 40% budget and 50% sparsity, Table 3 reports 80.59% for NMSGMP versus 80.94% for unstructured FiPS.

T1.justification: v2 removes Section 3's analytical rank/storage calculation, the F/D < 0.94 storage-saving condition, and the MAC-cost reasoning for factorized versus materialized execution. The core factorization mathematics, reconstruction loss, and Appendix A.1 formulations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction explicitly expands the compression contribution to both structured and unstructured sparsity while retaining the 25–40% parameter-budget and under-one-percentage-point accuracy-loss claim. The abstract and central claim about sharing neurons through sparse decomposition otherwise retain their meaning.

C2.justification: v2 adds deployment qualifications: efficient sparse operations are necessary, dedicated kernels are outside scope, and CSR indexing can increase memory overhead. It removes the earlier speculative discussion of materialization benefits in distributed or federated settings. Interpretations of the retained accuracy experiments remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 documents profiling hardware, DeepSparse, 16-bit tensor compatibility, and storage formats. It removes the FiPS source-code link and Sparsimony implementation disclosure; this establishes reduced access information, not that the resources became unavailable. Appendix optimizer and sparsifier settings are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references concerning structured sparsity and sparse execution, including Lasby et al., Lee et al., Zhou et al., Mishra et al., and Neural Magic. It removes Aghajanyan et al., Ström, and the Sparsimony citation. The central positioning relative to compression and parameter-sharing research remains similar.

P1.justification: Contribution bullets, selected ablation explanations, related work, and the conclusion are rewritten or condensed. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain intact, so these are targeted editorial revisions rather than a wholesale narrative reorganization.

P2.justification: v2 adds the three-panel profiling Figure 5 and structured-sparsity Table 3. Existing figures and tables are relocated or renumbered, and Figure 3's caption is expanded. Existing plot artwork and the general document and table styling are preserved.

improvement.justification: The new hardware measurements and structured-sparsity comparisons make practical compression benefits more assessable than v1's analytical discussion alone. These gains are tempered by removed code-access information and an overbroad revised contribution claim: Table 3's best structured result at a 40% budget is 80.59%, versus 81.85% originally, which does not support the claimed under-one-point loss.
